Box Plots

Source: vignettes/articles/r-docs/box-plots.Rmd
box-plots.Rmd

Basic Boxplot 

library(plotly.core)

go_figure() |>
  add_box(y = ~rnorm(50)) |>
  add_box(y = ~rnorm(50, 1))

Choosing The Algorithm For Computing Quartiles

By default, quartiles for box plots are computed using the linear method (for more about linear interpolation, see #10 listed on http://www.amstat.org/publications/jse/v14n3/langford.html and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quartile for more details).

However, you can also choose to use an exclusive or an inclusive algorithm to compute quartiles.

The exclusive algorithm uses the median to divide the ordered dataset into two halves. If the sample is odd, it does not include the median in either half. Q1 is then the median of the lower half and Q3 is the median of the upper half.

The inclusive algorithm also uses the median to divide the ordered dataset into two halves, but if the sample is odd, it includes the median in both halves. Q1 is then the median of the lower half and Q3 the median of the upper half.

library(plotly.core)

# or "inclusive", or "linear" by default
go_figure() |>
  add_box(y = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5), quartilemethod = "exclusive")

Modifying The Algorithm For Computing Quartiles

For an explanation of how each algorithm works, see Choosing The Algorithm For Computing Quartiles

library(plotly.core)

go_figure() |>
  add_box(
    y = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5),
    quartilemethod = "linear",
    name = "Linear Quartile Mode"
  ) |>
  add_box(
    y = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5),
    quartilemethod = "inclusive",
    name = "Inclusive Quartile Mode"
  ) |>
  add_box(
    y = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5),
    quartilemethod = "exclusive",
    name = "Exclusive Quartile Mode"
  ) |>
  update_layout(title = "Modifying The Algorithm For Computing Quartiles")

Box Plot With Precomputed Quartiles

You can specify precomputed quartile attributes rather than using a built-in quartile computation algorithm.

This could be useful if you have already pre-computed those values or if you need to use a different algorithm than the ones provided.

library(plotly.core)

go_figure() |>
  add_box(
    y = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9),
    q1 = c(1, 2, 3),
    median = c(4, 5, 6),
    q3 = c(7, 8, 9),
    lowerfence = c(-1, 0, 1),
    upperfence = c(5, 6, 7),
    mean = c(2.2, 2.8, 3.2),
    sd = c(0.2, 0.4, 0.6),
    notchspan = c(0.2, 0.4, 0.6)
  )

Horizontal Boxplot 

library(plotly.core)

go_figure() |>
  add_box(x = ~rnorm(50)) |>
  add_box(x = ~rnorm(50, 1))

Adding Jittered Points 

go_figure() |>
  add_box(y = ~rnorm(50), boxpoints = "all", jitter = 0.3, pointpos = -1.8)

Several Box Plots 

diamonds <- ggplot2::diamonds

diamonds |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_box(y = ~price, marker = go_box_marker(color = ~cut))

Grouped Box Plots 

diamonds <- ggplot2::diamonds

diamonds |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_box(x = ~cut, y = ~price, marker = go_box_marker(color = ~clarity)) |>
  update_layout(boxmode = "group")

Styling Outliers 

library(plotly.core)

y1 <- c(0.75, 5.25, 5.5, 6, 6.2, 6.6, 6.80, 7.0, 7.2, 7.5, 7.5, 7.75, 8.15,
       8.15, 8.65, 8.93, 9.2, 9.5, 10, 10.25, 11.5, 12, 16, 20.90, 22.3, 23.25)
y2 <- c(0.75, 5.25, 5.5, 6, 6.2, 6.6, 6.80, 7.0, 7.2, 7.5, 7.5, 7.75, 8.15,
        8.15, 8.65, 8.93, 9.2, 9.5, 10, 10.25, 11.5, 12, 16, 20.90, 22.3, 23.25)
y3 <- c(0.75, 5.25, 5.5, 6, 6.2, 6.6, 6.80, 7.0, 7.2, 7.5, 7.5, 7.75, 8.15,
        8.15, 8.65, 8.93, 9.2, 9.5, 10, 10.25, 11.5, 12, 16, 20.90, 22.3, 23.25)
y4 <- c(0.75, 5.25, 5.5, 6, 6.2, 6.6, 6.80, 7.0, 7.2, 7.5, 7.5, 7.75, 8.15,
        8.15, 8.65, 8.93, 9.2, 9.5, 10, 10.25, 11.5, 12, 16, 20.90, 22.3, 23.25)

go_figure() |>
  add_box(
    y = y1,
    jitter = 0.3,
    pointpos = -1.8,
    boxpoints = "all",
    marker = go_box_marker(color = "rgb(7,40,89)"),
    line = go_box_line(color = "rgb(7,40,89)"),
    name = "All Points"
  ) |>
  add_box(
    y = y2,
    name = "Only Whiskers",
    boxpoints = FALSE,
    marker = go_box_marker(color = "rgb(9,56,125)"),
    line = go_box_line(color = "rgb(9,56,125)")
  ) |>
  add_box(
    y = y3,
    name = "Suspected Outlier",
    boxpoints = "suspectedoutliers",
    marker = go_box_marker(
      color = "rgb(8,81,156)",
      outliercolor = "rgba(219, 64, 82, 0.6)",
      line = go_box_marker_line(
        outliercolor = "rgba(219, 64, 82, 1.0)",
        outlierwidth = 2
      )
    ),
    line = go_box_line(color = "rgb(8,81,156)")
  ) |>
  add_box(
    y = y4,
    name = "Whiskers and Outliers",
    boxpoints = "outliers",
    marker = go_box_marker(color = "rgb(107,174,214)"),
    line = go_box_line(color = "rgb(107,174,214)")
  ) |>
  update_layout(title = "Box Plot Styling Outliers")

Reference

See go_box() for more information and chart attribute options!
